1. Verify current bill arithmetic: confirm meter reads imply 1,615 kWh (18,705 − 17,090), line items sum to $277.94 ($18.38 + $42.49 + $217.07), and the month-over-month change is +$16.71 ($277.94 − $261.23). Treat any mismatch as a potential billing error.

2. Set price_usd: both billing periods fall under the same AEP Ohio RS tariff (fixed $18.38/month; tier-1 variable $0.0263125 + $0.13441 = $0.1607225/kWh for ≤2,000 kWh), so rates are unchanged → price_usd = $0.00.

3. Set days_usd: both periods are 31 days and the customer charge is a flat monthly fee rather than per-day, so day-count contributes nothing → days_usd = $0.00.

4. Estimate weather_usd: use the NOAA degree-day history to fit a weather-to-kWh relationship, isolate the weather-attributable kWh difference between last month (CDD 365, HDD 0) and the current period (CDD 210, HDD 24), and value those weather-driven kWh at the effective variable rate (~$0.1607/kWh).

5. Compute usage_usd as the residual so price_usd + days_usd + weather_usd + usage_usd equals exactly +$16.71 (i.e., value the non-weather portion of the 104 kWh increase at the variable rate).

6. Screen for a billing error: reconstruct the expected tariff total for 1,615 kWh ($18.38 + 1,615 × $0.1607225 ≈ $277.95), compare to the stated $277.94 and line items; the ~$0.01 gap is normal rounding, so billing_error_suspected = false and billing_error_usd = null.

7. Return only the JSON object with keys price_usd, days_usd, weather_usd, usage_usd, billing_error_suspected, and billing_error_usd.
